- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model should not overcorrect — cap forecast slope to avoid overshoot.
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is bearish, model should underpredict early in horizon to reflect supply constraints.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model should not assume linear trend — introduce mean reversion bias toward prior 7-day average if volatility exceeds 3%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model should avoid overfitting to recent highs — use 14-day moving average as baseline.
- For policy events (policy_count > 0), reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per event to reflect regulatory uncertainty.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from forecast in first 5 days, reset forecast anchor to 3-day SMA of true values to avoid lagged bias.
- In high-bearish sentiment (≤-0.33) with negative supply net, model should not forecast below 70% of prior 10-day low — avoid bottoming too early.
